checks.detail: R_lambda = sum_c eps_h(c) - F(n) against shape_terms' R for all 914 shapes with n <= 16: worst |difference| = 9.9568e-60 (tolerance 1.0e-45). Every ln q0 and ln(t-1) cancels identically; this is (I') of #7070 before the beta change of variables.

all 28628 partitions with n <= 30: #{c : h(c)=m} <= l for every m (0 violations) and R_lambda <= (l-1) C (0 violations, C = 6.17140572008). The prior chain used C r with r = min(l, lambda_1) and then r <= sqrt(H); this keeps l and prices the energy against l instead.

exact integers, all partitions n <= 30: row form (3) matches the cell hook sum (0 mismatches); (4) 2H >= l(l+1) + (n-l)(2j+1) - sum_(i<l)((j-1-i)_+)^2 for every 0 <= j <= n+1 (0 violations); (5) 2(H - H+) >= (l-k)^2 - r for l >= k (0 violations, equality in 30 cases, e.g. [(1, [1]), (2, [1, 1]), (3, [2, 1]), (4, [2, 1, 1])]); (5') 2(H - H+) >= -r + (k-l)(2k+1-2l)(k+1-l)/6 for l < k (0 violations). H+ = P_k + r(k+1) equals the brute-force H_min(n) and the committed closed form (0 mismatches), and H(lambda+) = H+ (0 mismatches).

n = 2..44, exact scan over p(n) shapes, 60 dps: M_n <= U_exact(rows) <= U_tangent <= U* <= (6') and REV_n <= M_n + log p(n) <= (6') + pi sqrt(2n/3) = (7) at every n (0 link failures); log p(n) <= pi sqrt(2n/3) at every n. At n=44: M=21.146195, REV=28.604269, U_exact=190.87117, U_tangent=198.17502, U*=226.12511, (6')=234.71994, (7)=251.73489. The bound is loose by a large constant (C^2/(2L) = 182.509) but its GROWTH is sqrt n, which is the claim.

(b) of the recovered block, re-measured with the Sigma-beta constraint enforced by enumeration and the pair term dropped (a valid relaxation of (I')): n=16: M_n=8.08015  B_sigma(no pair)=64.4252  recovered B_sigma=16.11  #7081=35.07 | n=24: M_n=12.4052  B_sigma(no pair)=101.344  recovered B_sigma=26.14  #7081=46.30 | n=32: M_n=16.2765  B_sigma(no pair)=133.061  recovered B_sigma=34.25  #7081=54.96 | n=40: M_n=19.7497  B_sigma(no pair)=159.037  recovered B_sigma=40.04  #7081=61.13 | n=44: M_n=21.1462  B_sigma(no pair)=169.738  recovered B_sigma=42.24  #7081=-. M_n <= B_sigma at every n, and the recovered (pair-term-kept) values sit below it as they must -- the pair term is most of the gap. B_sigma/M_n = n=41:8.05, n=42:8.0, n=43:8.018, n=44:8.027. None of this is needed for the proof; it cross-validates that enforcing Sigma-beta alone does not close the gap, which is why the route through (5) is the one that does.

at n=44 (k=8): Hhat_min(l) / exact min H over l-row shapes / H_min(n)=276: l=8: 235.086 / 276; l=16: 258.333 / 304; l=22: 339.429 / 373; l=24: 375.594 / 405. Hhat drops BELOW the global H_min(n) for 12 of the 42 row counts -- a negative 'energy' no partition has. At #7081's own n=4000 argmax l=151: Hhat_min = 116730.21 against H_min(4000) = 238520 (48.94 %). That credit is what made its relaxation's /n^(3/4) column rise; it is an artefact of the H lower bound used there, not evidence about REV_n. (5) has no such regime: its energy is >= -r/2.

(c) of the recovered block from the closed form (6), no enumeration: U*/sqrt n = n=44:34.089, n=100:25.703, n=200:20.797, n=1000:14.179, n=4000:11.444, n=10000:10.471, n=100000:9.3142, n=1000000:8.9491; limit (C + L/2) sqrt2 = 8.8014657, approached from above within (C^2/(2L) + C)/sqrt n = 188.68/sqrt n at every n; U*/n^(3/4) = 13.236, 8.1281, 5.5302, 2.5215, 1.4390, 1.0471, 0.5237, 0.2829 -> 0. The integer argmax is x = l - k = 59 at every n (C/L = 59.1467), matching the l - sqrt(2n) = 62 drift #7081 saw at n = 4000 and could not explain.
